title: Usage is not satisfaction or causal value
assessment: High smart-TV usage supports relevance of the touchpoint but does not establish that the screen caused satisfaction, loyalty, or revenue.
resolution: Keep 62% as a direct fact and show value pathways as supported inferences or property-specific scenarios.

title: Announced capability is not universal availability
assessment: Samsung disclosures specify model, region, language, channel, software, device, and separate-licensing limitations.
resolution: Label all capabilities vendor-stated, surface limitations in the explorer, and avoid universal wording.

title: Current guidance is not new 2026 measurement
assessment: The ENERGY STAR page is current, but the benchmark context should not be described as newly measured in 2026.
resolution: Describe the figures as current agency guidance and require verified property baselines for savings scenarios.

title: Industry scale is not screen-attributable value
assessment: Hotel spending and global Travel and Tourism GDP describe the surrounding economy, not the revenue created by connected displays.
resolution: Use $805B only as economic context in the carousel and keep $11.6T in the explorer or a small note.

title: Autonomous does not mean no human governance
assessment: Humans establish the charter, approve publication, and govern risk even when agents conduct bounded research stages.
resolution: Use ‘AI-led, evidence-audited research with disclosed human governance’ and record review actions in the run manifest.

title: Translation is not full accessibility
assessment: Live translation can reduce language friction but does not satisfy the broader needs of captions, text alternatives, programmatic relationships, focus, contrast, and input accessibility.
resolution: Keep translation as one vendor-stated example and provide accessible non-graph navigation in HXG itself.
